what_its_for: Sodium supplements are used to replace low sodium levels in your body (a condition called hyponatremia). Your doctor may also prescribe them if you lose a lot of sodium through heavy sweating, certain medical conditions, or some medications. Sodium helps your body control fluid balance, nerve signals, and muscle function.
how_to_take: Take sodium tablets or capsules by mouth with a full glass of water (at least 8 ounces). You may take them with food or milk to help avoid an upset stomach. Do not crush or chew extended-release tablets — swallow them whole. Follow your doctor's instructions exactly, as taking too much sodium can be harmful.
dosing: Your dose will be set by your doctor based on your blood sodium levels and your health condition. A common adult dose may range from 1 to 2 grams (1,000–2,000 mg) taken 3 times a day, but your dose may be very different. Never adjust your dose on your own without talking to your doctor or pharmacist first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store sodium tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep them away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid adding extra salt to your food unless your doctor tells you to. Limit foods very high in sodium (like canned soups, processed meats, and fast food) unless directed otherwise. Avoid taking antacids or other sodium-containing products without checking with your doctor, as they may add too much sodium. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some drugs can interact with sodium.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden swelling in your hands, feet, or ankles; difficulty breathing or shortness of breath; severe headache, confusion, or seizures; muscle weakness, cramps, or irregular heartbeat; nausea, vomiting, or feeling very unwell; or signs of too much sodium such as extreme thirst, restlessness, or decreased urination. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve or get worse.
when_it_works: Sodium supplements can start to raise your blood sodium levels within a few hours, but it may take several days of treatment before you feel noticeably better. Your doctor will check your blood sodium levels regularly with blood tests to make sure the treatment is working safely. Never stop taking this medication without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to changes in sodium levels and are at higher risk for fluid retention and high blood pressure. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before taking sodium supplements, as excess sodium may affect you and your baby. People with heart disease, kidney disease, or high blood pressure: Use only under close medical supervision, as extra sodium can worsen these conditions. Children: Dosing must be carefully determined by a doctor based on the child's weight and sodium levels.
